rule.verified: A relationship is marked verified (CONFIRMED) only when a DOCUMENTED fact is stated by one of its two companies in its own regulatory filing, investor-relations or newsroom release, or official product/engineering page, and the https source link passes the automated link check on the review date.
rule.notVerified: Announced or planned activity, third-party reporting, and facts not yet re-checked are never marked verified. Needs verification is reserved for facts an editor explicitly marks PENDING.

companies.name: SK hynix
companies.description: Korean memory manufacturer supplying DRAM, NAND and high-bandwidth memory (HBM) used in AI accelerators. Named by NVIDIA as a memory supplier.

companies.name: Samsung Electronics
companies.description: Korean electronics company whose semiconductor business makes memory, including HBM, and provides foundry manufacturing. Named by NVIDIA as a wafer and memory supplier.

companies.name: Hon Hai (Foxconn)
companies.legalName: Hon Hai Precision Industry Co., Ltd.
companies.description: Taiwanese contract manufacturer (Foxconn). NVIDIA names it as a contract manufacturer for assembly, testing and packaging. Its A-share subsidiary Foxconn Industrial Internet (601138) is listed separately.

companies.name: Wistron
companies.description: Taiwanese electronics manufacturer. NVIDIA names it as a contract manufacturer for assembly, testing and packaging.

companies.name: Quanta Computer
companies.description: Taiwanese computer and cloud-server manufacturer. Its subsidiary Quanta Cloud Technology (QCT) builds rack-scale NVIDIA systems.

sources.title: NVIDIA Form 10-K for fiscal year 2026 (Manufacturing)
sources.excerpt: Manufacturing: foundries such as TSMC and Samsung produce NVIDIA semiconductor wafers; NVIDIA purchases memory from SK Hynix, Micron and Samsung; contract manufacturers such as Hon Hai Precision Industry, Wistron and Fabrinet perform assembly, testing and packaging of final products.

sources.title: Broadcom Form 10-K for fiscal year 2025 (Manufacturing)
sources.excerpt: Front-end wafer manufacturing is largely outsourced to foundries including TSMC (about 95% of contract-manufactured wafers in fiscal 2025); assembly and test contractors include TSMC, ASE, Foxconn Technology Group, Amkor and SPIL.

sources.title: CoreWeave Form 10-K for fiscal year 2025 (Suppliers)
sources.excerpt: CoreWeave depends on a limited number of suppliers for its infrastructure; its GPUs are supplied principally by NVIDIA.

sources.title: Microsoft Azure delivers the first large-scale cluster with NVIDIA GB300 NVL72
sources.excerpt: Azure NDv6 GB300 VM series: a production cluster of more than 4,600 NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs in GB300 NVL72 systems.

sources.title: Amazon EC2 P6-B200 instances powered by NVIDIA B200 GPUs now generally available
sources.excerpt: EC2 P6-B200 instances with eight NVIDIA Blackwell B200 GPUs are generally available.

sources.title: New A4X VMs powered by NVIDIA GB200 GPUs | Google Cloud Blog
sources.excerpt: Google Cloud A4X VMs run on NVIDIA GB200 NVL72; A4 VMs run on NVIDIA HGX B200.

sources.title: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Deploys Thousands of NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs for Agentic AI and Reasoning Models
